During the hearing of the review petition on 6.2.2025, through virtual hearing, the learned counsel for the Review Petitioner and the learned counsel for the Respondent argued the matter at length. The Commission, after permitting the parties to file their short note of arguments, reserved its order in the review petition. In compliance thereof, the Review Petitioner and the Respondent NTPC have filed their note of arguments on proceed to examine the issue raised in the review petition in the subsequent paragraphs. - b) The Hon’ble Supreme Court in a catena of judgments held that a review petition cannot be used to reargue the merits of evidence, effectively transforming the review into an appeal. A review is not a rehearing of the original matter; it cannot correct all errors like an appellate authority can. It is only for exceptional cases and must be approached with caution. The prayers sought by the Review Petitioner are beyond the scope of the powers conferred by the Courts under Review jurisdiction. Thus, only on this ground, the present Petition should be dismissed at the very threshold. - c) The Review Petitioner has not approached this Commission with clean hands and has disclosed that various appeals have been filed by the Review Petitioner before the APTEL, thereby raising a similar ground. However, the same is for a different generating station, but the principal issue challenged therein is the same. The Review Petitioner has indulged in forum shopping and has also raised a similar issue in Appeal No. 258/2022 filed by it before the APTEL. - d) The issue raised by the Review Petitioner in the present petition qua the IoWC on the basis of ‘as billed’ GCV of coal for the period of January 2014, to March 2014 is an issue which falls for consideration in Appeal No. 258/2022. Notably, all the appeals in question have been filed by the Review Petitioner before the APTEL. When an issue which is _sub judice_ before a superior court, the lower court must refrain from considering the said issue till the adjudication of the matter in its entirety by the superior court. Therefore, the present petition is not maintainable at all. - k) The orders passed by this Commission in various petitions involve different stations of the Respondent, the details of which are as follows: Xxx From a perusal of the above list of orders passed by this Commission, it is clear that this Commission has taken a consistent view with regard to the issue at hand. Therefore, the present Petition cannot be given a different position as it would be bad and perverse, as this Commission had already decided the said issue for several other stations of the Respondent in the aforesaid petitions. It is not error apparent when the Courts are taking a consistent view in different matters - q) In fact, this Commission _vide_ its order dated 19.2.2016 in Petition No. 33/MP/ 2014, decided the fate of the subject matter involved herein and held as under: - r) In view of the above order, it is clear that the present dispute does not require any intervention of this Commission, as the view put forth by this Commission is clear and is applicable to the Review Petitioner. 8. In response to the above, the Review Petitioner vide its rejoinder affidavit dated i) The objections raised by NTPC to the maintainability of the Review Petition is misconceived and untenable. The impugned order dated 11.1.2024 to the extent of computation of IoWC on the basis of ‘as received’ data of GCV of coal for the months of January 2014, February 2014 and March 2014 submitted by NTPC suffers from ‘errors apparent’ and also falls under the expression ‘for any other sufficient reason’ in Order 47 Rule 1 CPC as interpreted by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the judgments, viz., BCCI vs. Netaji Cricket Club (2005) 4 SCC 741; and Lily Thomas vs. Union of India (2000) 6 SCC 224. 10. Before proceeding to consider the issue raised by the Review Petitioner, we examine the submissions of NTPC that he present petition is not maintainable, on the count that the issue raised by the Review Petitioner in the present petition, qua the IoWC on the basis of ‘as billed’ GCV of coal for the period of January, 2014, to March, 2014 is an issue which falls for consideration in Appeal No. 258/2022 filed by the Review Petitioner before APTEL and that when an issue which is _sub judice_ before a superior court, the lower court must refrain itself from considering the said issue till the adjudication of the matter in its entirety by the superior court. _Per contra_ , the Review Petitioner has argued that the Review Petition is maintainable, since there is no bar against the filing of an Appeal and a Review Petition against the different orders of the Commission and for different generating stations of NTPC, even if the issues involved is the same. (Farakka STPS) involved in the Review Petition. As rightly pointed out by the Review Petitioner, even if the issues involved are the same, there is no bar for the filing and consideration of an appeal and a Review Petition in respect of the different orders of the Commission for different generating stations of NTPC. There is also no interim order/directions of the superior court (APTEL), in the present case, barring the Commission from considering the said issue, which has been raised in the Review Petition. In this backdrop, we find no reason to reject the review petition as not maintainable, on this count. Accordingly, we proceed to examine whether the issue raised by the Review Petitioner is maintainable on merits, as stated in the subsequent paragraphs. its power of review. These principles of review have also been enunciated by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in its judgment in Kamlesh Verma Vs. Mayawati and ors (AIR 2006 SC 75). In the above background, the submissions of the Review Petitioner are rejected, and the Review Petition is rejected as not maintainable.
